subject: bauhausBird
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: songbird on a branch.
Style: Bauhaus primary-colour geometry.
reasoning:
I'm planning a Bauhaus-style songbird module using primary colors and geometric primitives like spheres, cones, and boxes, with a branch built from a sweep and joints to rig the small ~0.15m creature.

Working out the skeleton now: a hip root joint with spine chain through chest, neck, head, plus beak joints, a tail chain, wing chains from shoulder joints, and leg chains with toes, positioning each at specific coordinates to perch naturally on the branch.

Still shaping wing geometry...

Mapping out the bird's components by color and shape: blue body sphere, red breast, yellow head sphere, black beak cones, white/black eye discs, boxy tail segments in blue/black/yellow, red wings with black stripes, a small black crest on the crown, thin black legs with toe boxes, and a dark branch beam with accent rings.

Now I'm working out exact dimensions and joint positions -- body sphere size and center, leg rod endpoints running from body to branch top, toe placement -- making sure bones exist before I attach parts to them, then starting to write the construction code.

Defining head, chest, and beak geometry...

Now I'm placing a black crown cone tilted back on the head with a red crest accent, then building the tail from boxes—a central blue feather chain with two flanking yellow feathers rotated outward at slight yaw angles.

For props, I'm setting up a simple root joint for the branch and body since they don't need full rigging, then sweeping a polyline from one side to the other with a flat circular cross-section to form the branch, adding an angled twig extending upward from it.

For the leaf I'm placing a yellow disc and a red triangular extrusion at the twig's end, and for the wings I'm positioning extruded shapes along the body's surface, with yellow stripe details and a red circle accent layered on top, all centered using mirrored thickness along the X axis.

Now I'm setting up the skeletal chains: wing joints named by side with a shoulder position, and leg chains with hip, knee, and ankle points defined as a short polyline so the third point forms the ankle tip bone.
